scope.basis: The current delivery changes the HTML brand wordmark's vertical scroll relationship to the rendered product.

claims.statement: At hero start and 30% scroll, the single HTML wordmark remains a coherent horizontal brand field with an intentional vertical relationship to the product rather than an accidental top-edge crop.
claims.consumer: desktop visitor reviewing the control-valve product story

evidence_strategies.target: 1280x800 local range-preview page at scroll progress 0 and 0.30
evidence_strategies.probe: Playwright screenshot with scroll travel derived from .video-scroll-shell

coverage.reason: Direct screenshots were captured and visually reviewed at both requested scroll states after the timing adjustment.

evidence.summary: The complete wordmark is centered at y=280px to y=408px; the product's vertical axis crosses the brand field without clipping the viewport.
The complete wordmark remains visible at y=77px to y=205px with opacity 0.78125 and maintains an intentional overlap with the upper product axis.

findings.subject: HTML wordmark scroll timing
findings.observed: Before the adjustment, the 30% wordmark top was -4px, leaving the field mostly cropped. After changing the upward-motion interval from [0.08, 0.80] to [0.16, 0.80], its top is 77px at 30% while its exit remains complete by 80%.
findings.expected: The brand field remains visibly and intentionally related to the product through the early motion beat, then leaves the viewport during the later story.
findings.impact: The early product story retains a stable brand anchor instead of presenting an abrupt, accidental-looking title loss.
reproduction: Set page scroll to the video-scroll-shell travel multiplied by 0.30 and capture again.
